c.tagline: Venetian old town, twin fortresses, and the Ionian's greenest island.

taxi.fareNote: Ride-hailing apps like Uber and Bolt are effectively unavailable on Corfu; you hail metered taxis at ranks or phone/radio-book them. Confirm the fare or zone tariff for out-of-town trips, and expect a 25-30% surcharge for late-night rides.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance, with English-speaking operators.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Kavos and other party resorts see alcohol-fuelled trouble at night, and Corfu Town's crowded lanes draw occasional pickpockets in high season.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed Venetian heart of Corfu Town, a maze of narrow kantounia (alleys), the arcaded Liston, Spianada square and the two fortresses; best for first-timers who want history, cafes, and sights on foot.

A scenic seaside neighborhood just south of the Old Town with a 2 km promenade from the Old Fortress to the Windmill, leafy parkland and some of the island's finest tavernas; a peaceful, villagey base with an authentic local feel.

The green, lush peninsula south of town, once the island's original capital, famed for the view over Mouse Island (Pontikonisi) and the Vlacherna monastery; a calm area of mid-sized resort hotels close to the airport.

Corfu Town's working port district north of the center, home to the ferry harbor, budget rooms and lively local tavernas and bars; handy for early ferries and travelers wanting an unpolished, affordable base.
A relaxed coastal suburb north of town with a yacht marina, small beaches and family resorts, linked to the center by frequent blue buses; good for a quieter, greener stay with easy town access.

water.note: Tap water quality varies around the island; most visitors drink bottled.

transit.hours: Blue town buses run roughly 6:00am to 10:00-11:00pm; green intercity buses run mostly daytime with sparse evening service, so late nights rely on taxis.
transit.note: Corfu has no metro, tram or rail. Two bus networks cover the island: blue urban buses around Corfu Town and its suburbs, and green KTEL coaches to the rest of the island.
transit.pay: Pay the driver or conductor in cash on board. Blue urban buses around Corfu Town cost roughly €1.20-1.70 a ride; the green KTEL intercity buses to island villages and resorts are priced by distance, bought at the bus station or on board. There is no contactless or rechargeable card system.

transit.m: Blue Bus line 15 to San Rocco Square / town (~10-15 min)
Taxi to Corfu Town center (~10 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated.

food.name: Pastitsada
food.desc: Corfu's Sunday dish: rooster or veal braised for hours in tomato, red wine and a Venetian spice mix heavy on cinnamon and clove, served over thick pasta.

food.name: Sofrito
food.desc: Thin veal escalopes stewed slowly with a lot of garlic, parsley and white wine vinegar until meltingly soft. The most Venetian dish on the island.

places.name: Rouvas

places.name: Taverna Tripa

food.name: Bourdeto
food.desc: Scorpion fish or cod simmered in a fierce red sauce of paprika, cayenne and olive oil. Genuinely spicy, which is unusual for Greek cooking.

places.name: Golden Fox

food.desc: The mild counterpart to bourdeto: white fish poached with potatoes, huge amounts of garlic, lemon juice, olive oil and black pepper, no tomato at all.

places.name: Nikolas Taverna

places.name: The Fisherman's Cabin

food.name: Kumquat spoon sweets
food.desc: Whole kumquats preserved in syrup and served as a glyko tou koutaliou with coffee or yoghurt. The fruit was introduced to Corfu in the 19th century.

places.name: Mavromatis Kumquat
places.note: Established Corfiot producer selling preserves and liqueur direct from its shop.

places.name: Corfu Town Old Market
places.note: Sweet shops around the Liston and Agora stock kumquat glyko and mandolato nougat.

places.name: Kafesas

food.name: Kumquat liqueur
food.desc: Bright orange liqueur distilled from the island's kumquats, sweet and faintly bitter, poured as a small digestif at the end of a taverna meal.

places.name: Mavromatis Kumquat

places.name: Liston arcade cafes

places.name: Taverna Tripa

food.name: Tsitsibira
food.desc: Corfiot ginger beer, a leftover of the 19th-century British protectorate and made nowhere else in Greece. Cloudy, sharp and lightly fizzy.

landmarks: Old Fortress (Palaio Frourio)
This mighty Venetian sea fortress on a rocky promontory guards Corfu Town across a moat, crowned by a lighthouse with sweeping Ionian views.
Corfu Old Town and the Liston
A UNESCO-listed Venetian labyrinth of tall shuttered houses opens onto the arcaded Liston promenade, built under French rule and made for evening strolling.
Achilleion Palace
Empress Sisi of Austria's melancholy neoclassical retreat above Gastouri brims with Achilles statuary and terraced gardens gazing over the emerald island.
Vlacherna Monastery and Pontikonisi (Mouse Island)
A tiny white monastery tethered to Kanoni by a causeway, with cypress-tufted Mouse Island floating behind, composing Corfu's most famous postcard.
Spianada Square
Greece's largest square spreads between the Old Fortress and the Liston, a French-planned expanse where locals still play cricket beneath Venetian facades.
Church of Saint Spyridon
The red-domed campanile of Corfu's patron saint towers over the old town, sheltering his silver reliquary, paraded through the streets four times yearly.
Angelokastro
A Byzantine eagle's-nest castle clinging to a 300-meter sea cliff above Paleokastritsa, never conquered and delivering hair-raising views along the west coast.
Kanoni viewpoint
The cafe-lined terrace above the old airport runway frames Vlacherna and Mouse Island while jets skim startlingly low over the lagoon.
Palace of St. Michael and St. George (Museum of Asian Art)
The British-built Regency palace at the Spianada's edge houses Greece's only museum of Asian art, with 15,000 works from Japan to India.
New Fortress (Neo Frourio)
A 16th-century Venetian stronghold on the Hill of Agios Markos above the old port, its tunnels and ramparts still marked by the winged lion of St. Mark.

train.note: There is no railway on Corfu - Hellenic Train (https://www.hellenictrain.gr/en) serves only the Greek mainland, and its international services to Bulgaria and North Macedonia remain suspended. Arrive by ferry from Igoumenitsa or Italy, or fly into Corfu airport.

intl.to: Athens & Thessaloniki (Greece) - through coaches including the ferry crossing

bus.note: There are no true international coaches, but the mainland services are unusual in that the coach itself boards the ferry at Igoumenitsa - Athens takes about 8-9 hours including the crossing. On the island, green KTEL buses run from the Corfu Town terminal to Paleokastritsa, Kassiopi and Sidari, and blue local buses cover the suburbs. Book the Athens coach ahead in summer.

intl.op: Kerkyra Lines / Lefkimmi Lines — tickets at the Corfu port

intl.to: Brindisi, Bari, Ancona & Venice (Italy) - overnight, mainly Apr-Oct

ferry.note: Corfu has two genuine international crossings: the year-round hydrofoil to Saranda in Albania, which takes half an hour and is a full border crossing needing your passport, and the seasonal Italy ferries which call here on the Igoumenitsa-Brindisi and Venice routes. The mainland shuttle to Igoumenitsa runs many times a day. Italy sailings are heavily reduced outside the April-October season.
